title: Bridgewell Utility Line Protection Plans Terms: Renewal, Expiry, Cancellation and Refund of Premium
content:
# Renewal, Expiry, Cancellation and Refund of Premium

**Plan terms, Bridgewell Utility Line Protection Plans.**

## 1. Renewal and expiry

1.1 A plan with automatic renewal on renews on its term end only when its renewal notice was issued at least the plan's renewal notice lead time in calendar days before the term end date; counting runs backward from the term end date and a notice issued exactly that many days before qualifies.

1.2 Otherwise the plan expires at the end of the term end date unless the customer renews before then.

1.3 An expired plan can be restored within the plan's late-renewal grace period in calendar days after the term end date with no new waiting period, starting a new term on the restoration date.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, a 30-day lead time assumed):* for a term ending on 30 June, counting back 30 days gives 31 May. A renewal notice issued on 31 May qualifies; a notice first issued on 1 June, 29 days before, does not.

## 2. Cancellation

2.1 The customer may cancel at any time by giving notice; the cancellation is effective on the notice date.

2.2 Within the plan's free-look period in calendar days after the start date, the customer is credited all premium paid less the benefit paid in the term. The days since start are counted from the day after the start date through the notice date inclusive.

2.3 After that, an annual-billed plan is credited the premium paid in the term times the unexpired days of the term divided by the days of the term, rounded to the cent, less the cancellation administrative fee and less the benefit paid in the term; and a monthly-billed plan is credited nothing and simply stops billing.

2.4 A credit is never negative. Only one cancellation credit is posted per plan cancellation.

2.5 Credits are refunded within the plan's refund period in calendar days to the channel that paid, a utility-billed plan being refunded by the partner utility as a bill credit.

## Quantities used in clause 2

| Quantity | How it is counted |
|---|---|
| Premium paid in the term | payments posted in the current term up to the cancellation notice date, less returned payment charges in that window |
| Benefit paid in the term | repair authorization amounts for service requests placed in the current term up to the notice date, less reversals of them |
| Unexpired days of the term | calendar days from the day after the notice date through the term end date, inclusive |
| Days of the term | calendar days from the term start date through the term end date, inclusive |
| Days since start | calendar days from the day after the start date through the notice date, inclusive |

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

- *Free-look:* a plan started on 1 March and cancelled by notice on 31 March has 30 days since start (2 March through 31 March). With a 30-day free-look period it is within the period; premium paid of $60.00 and benefit paid of $0.00 give a credit of $60.00. Notice on 1 April would be day 31, outside the period.
- *Annual-billed, after free-look:* premium paid $120.00, a 365-day term, 146 unexpired days, an administrative fee of $5.00 and benefit paid of $20.00. $120.00 times 146 divided by 365 is $48.00; less $5.00 and less $20.00, the credit is $23.00.
- *Annual-billed, benefit larger than the prorated premium:* if the benefit paid were $60.00 in the same case, the amount would fall below zero, and the credit is $0.00.
- *Monthly-billed, after free-look:* no credit is posted; billing stops.
